newsitem.title: USA: Russian delays may unravel space station - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Russian delays may unravel space station - NYT.

text.p: The new chairman of the House Science Committee criticized Russia's delays in the effort to build an international space station, saying the project could be derailed, the New York Times said Monday.

James Sensenbrenner told the paper that the danger of the program unraveling is great and said Russia should be asked to leave as full partners in the project if it is still withholding payments at the end of February.
The Russian module is to serve as the early control center and living quarters for the $50 billion station, but the module is nearly a year behind schedule, the paper said.
In December NASA decided to build an interim module to handle some functions of the Russian module until it is built.
The report said NASA officials believe Russia's problems can be overcome but also are studying a second makeshift component that would serve the station if Russia's module is never made.
Fifteen nations are working on the space station.
The paper said recent problems could delay the first permanent inhabitation of the space station by half a year.
